back: The branch of computer science dealing with the simulation of intelligent behaviour by computers.
A collection of data and rules for using it; the ability to reason; (in some systems) the ability to learn and adapt.
AI system using expert knowledge (knowledge base + rule base) and an inference engine to give advice in a narrow field, with an explanation.
Knowledge base (facts), rule base (IF … THEN rules), inference engine (applies rules), interface (questions in, conclusion and explanation out).
The part of an expert system that applies the rules to the facts and the user's answers to reach a conclusion and choose the next question.
AI in which a program automatically adapts its own processes and/or data from experience, without being reprogrammed.
Medical diagnosis, plant and animal disease identification, mineral prospecting, car fault diagnosis, financial advice, chess.
Spam filters, recommendations, face and speech recognition, predictive text, fraud detection.

front: Advantages and disadvantages of expert systems
back: + expertise anywhere, consistent, explains reasoning. − costly to build, only as good as its knowledge, no common sense, needs updating.
